Ah, estate sales, got it.
Then we can come back, hit a few places here and then grab some lunch.
Do we have time for coffee now? I haven't had any for hours.
For hours? When did you get up?
Five.
Wow, they have one of those in the morning too?
You know how Asia is not taking the morning off? Neither is Europe.
Well, coffee, it is then.
How about you taking me to that place you're always talking about. What is it, um - Duke's.
[chuckles] Duke's. Sure. Or, uh, we could go some place else.
Why? Why not Duke's?
It's not so special.
You go there daily.
Yeah, but I think Duke's is closed… and it's Luke's.
Closed at eight in the morning on a Friday?
Yeah. Sabbath.
Duke's a Jew.
No, Luke's a Jew.
Sabbath's not 'til sundown.
Well, he likes to get an early jump on his - Sabbathing.
I bet he's open.
Okay, but we run the risk of going and then discovering it's closed.
Well, I say live dangerously or not at all.
Yeah. Yeah, you're right. All the other coffee in town sucks. Let's just go to Duke's - which is Luke's.
Which is Luke's?
[grinning] Dukes.
What? [Lorelai giggles]
No, no Rietgaard, those documents were Fed-Ex'd to you on Wednesday. Uh, the dok-umen-ten were Fed-Ex'd, on - aw, sh**t, on… Monday is maandag, Tuesday is dinsdag… [to Lorelai] How's your Dutch?
Oh great. I just don't like to share it.
I'll just have the office fax it all over to you today. It's okay.
Hey, is he ice-skating under a windmill, that's the picture I have in my head.
Okay, Rietgaard, good bye. Bye. [closes cell phone and sighs] I am exhausted.
Aww, and on your morning off!
Yeah, I stink at taking mornings off.
Well, here we are. [she pulls up in front of Luke's diner and turns off Jeep]
Ahh, wait.[A pause as he recognizes Luke's green truck across the street]
No more calls.
Whose truck is that? [pointing] Duke's?
Yeah, Luke's.
Are they different people?
Same person.
And that's his truck.
Yes, it's practically an appendage.
[Indicating the familiar diner owner through the window] Sooooo, that would be Luke.
Boy, you sure like to do a lot of research before getting a cup of coffee. That's the doorknob. It twists to the right. C'mon. [starts to remove safety belt]
Ahhh -
What is with you?
Yeah, I'm not in the mood for coffee anymore.
[gasps at the obvious lie] You were jonesing not 5 minutes ago.
No, it's passed. My 5 a.m. coffee just kicked in again.
You drink time-released coffee?
[shrugs] It's all the rage.
Okay. Well, I want coffee. [pulls off safety belt and prepares to get out]
Okay, I'll wait for you here.
What is with you?
[Pause] I-I was kind of tailgating Duke on the drive in.
You were tailgating Luke?
Pretty rudely. There was honking.
Aw, geez.
Well, I didn't know it was Duke.
How fast was he going?
Snail's speed. Like twenty.
The speed limit here is twelve!

Okay See this is one of the problems I have with small towns - proximity. [During Jason's rant, Luke looks out the window, recognizes Lorelai's jeep out front. Looking closer he sees a man sitting next to her] You tailgate a guy in Manhattan and you never see him again, you tailgate a guy in a small town, he is the keeper of the coffee. [He looks over at the diner window]. And he is looking at us!
Who Luke?
Is that his name?
YES! [she peers past Jason to see Luke]
Okay, don't look at him! Don't look at him!
This is ridiculous!
Okay go, go, go! [motions for her to drive away]
Where?!
Anywhere - else - for coffee, please.
Okay. [starts up the engine and drives 5 feet and stops]
Why are we stopping?
Um, the next best place for coffee is at this place. [pointing to the next building]
Okay Please find us coffee at least fifty yards away from Duke's.
[mocking] Oh, oh okay finding coffee fifty yards from Luke's is another matter. [they drive away]
Hey Rory.
Oh, Jamie, hi.
Sorry to pounce on you like that.
That's okay, you're not pouncing. Wanna sit? [she sets her lunch tray on table]
Thanks. [they both sit] Listen, do you - ?
Do I what?
Look, I need to find out what's up with Paris, and I don't know who else to ask.
Oh.
I mean, I had to rearrange a million things to come here, and I could only manage two days and she won't see me.
Well, you're going to see her tomorrow, aren't you?
If she doesn't cancel.
She's not going to cancel. [Jamie gives her a doubtful look] She wouldn't.
Well, she's been canceling plans for weeks. She's not calling me as much - I know, I sound pathetic.
No you don't, and Paris has been so busy. You've been a freshman in college, you know what that entails.
Yeah. [unconvinced]
Plus, I heard her telling you about my friend, Lane. She's been living in our suite and it's been really unfair to all my roommates.
What is "chasing the dragon?"
I don't know, but that's what Lane says she's been doing. She's in cold turkey now - going it, I mean - cold turkey and -- um -- Paris has been really great helping out.
Has she been seeing someone else?
[shrugs] Not that I know of.
[smiles and rises to go] I'll let you go. Thanks, this actually helped.
Good. It will get better, Jamie. I really think that.
Good. [backs away] It's my birthday.
Oh wow, happy birthday.
Thanks. [Jamie turns and leaves. Rory watches him walk away]
[He hands change to the customer who leaves] Thanks. [walks to the opposite end of the counter and rests his head on the cool surface. The mystery woman enters the diner from the back stairs.]
Hey!
[startled] Oh yeah.
You forget about me?
No, I'm just real, real busy, that's all.
[looks around] Looks like a lull to me.
No, it can be deceptive. Hey, Kirk, you want another piece of pie?

No, I'm fine. And this is the commencement of your classic mid-morning lull. People off to work, kids off to school. You may not have another soul in here for half an hour. It gets peaceful, quiet - kind of like a sweet death.
[murmurs] He's trippy.
Kirk, are you sure you don't want anything else?
A spider monkey, but there is probably nothing you can do about it.
Cool. C'mon. [disappears behind the drape to go back upstairs]
Coming sis. [slowly follows her]
[He enters, closes the door and looks around] Liz? Liz?
[her call is muffled and off camera] I'm in the closet. Oh my God. It's still here.
What's still there?
My pot.
Your what?
I used to stash it in a hole back behind Daddy's files cause it was the one place he wouldn't look. Isn't that wild? It's still here.
[snatches it from her] Will you give me that.
Relax, will ya. I don't do that any more. [Luke stuffs it in a kitchen drawer] What are you doing?
I'm putting it away.
Throw it in the trash.
So the garbage man can see it?
Isn't Hayward Donnelly still the garbage man?
Yes.
Well hell, he sold it to me.
I'll get rid of it, okay Liz?
Okay, Luke. [she smiles at him] Boy, you look good. What about me, don't I look good?
[looks uncomfortable] You look fine.
I do not look fine, I look good. I am good. I am really good, Luke.
Well, I'm glad.
[indicates the table] I made us some coffee.
I don't drink coffee.

[urges him to sit] Well, sit down and watch me drink it then. Come on, just for a minute. [Luke sits down with Liz and silently watches her pour coffee] Look at us - catching up, and all. I haven't seen you in two years.
Three years.
Three years, wow.
Liz, I gotta know why you're here.
To see you, I've missed you.
C'mon.
I did, plus it's my twentieth high school reunion this Saturday, I thought I'd maybe come back and I'd check out what the rest of the class of 84's up to.
You're going to your high school reunion?

I even sent in a picture for the program. Wrote a little thing about myself, about how things are going good, I've got a great job, I've just moved into a really cool apartment with a big patio so I can finally get a dog. Plus, I have got -
Wait, wait, wait - let me guess. A new, a new boyfriend!
Yes!
And this one - Oh, let me guess - is different from the others.
Yes, he is.
I dare say, that he might even be the one!
Well, yeah!
[he stands and opens the refrigerator] C'mon, Liz.
You should meet him.
Well you know what? As long as, unlike the others, he leaves your TV when he takes off, I'll love him.
Okay, fine. You have good reason to think, to doubt -

Good reasons? Liz, every time you find the one you wind up with your bank account cleaned out, your stuff missing, crying on the phone to me to bail you out, which I do happily, but you'll understand if I hold off on planning for the bachelor party for a while. [pours orange juice and takes a drink from his glass]
Sure. Well - anyway - let's talk about something else.
Yes. Let's talk about something else. You said you had a new job.
Yes, I do. I do. I'm making my own jewelry: beaded necklaces and earrings, some crystal, getting into feathers now.
Feathers?
I'm really good, very big on the renaissance fair circuit.
What's that?

That's where I sell them, the renaissance fair circuit. It's a total trip. I wear the long skirt, I have a hat and one of those corsets that squishes my boobs all up high. And I yell "Huzza for the tipper!"
And that's your great new job? You sell earrings at the renaissance fair?
I know it sounds flaky -
Oh no, what - huzzah for the tipper with your squished up boobs, not flaky at all. Look, I have to go back to work.
Luke, come on.
What come on, Liz? I mean, you're selling earrings in a booth and you're hooked up with another winner.
You don't even know him.
What about your son, huh? What about Jess, you talk to him lately? You notice he's not even here?
Yeah, he sent me a letter. He's with his father.
That's it? That's the extent of the contact?
He's nineteen, you can't tell him anything.
Well, you definitely can't if you don't try.
I tried.
No, I tried, you gave up.
I thought you'd be better for him that I was.
Oh yeah, I was great for him. I gave him a place to crash while he lied to me about everything, about going to school, about Wal-Mart - you know I stole his car?
You what?
In the middle of the night. I break into his car. I'm stealing it and hiding it in Dad's old garage.
[chuckling] Why?

Why? Because I'm crazy. Because I think now he'll have to go to school, now he'll have to graduate, now - [sigh] well, we saw how that all turned out, he went to live with the bum who abandoned him - that's how great a job I did. [he sighs deeply and takes a gulp of his orange juice]
You tried.
Well, I'm great at trying aren't I? [deep sigh]
Well, I know you have a lot of work to do, so I'm gonna go. [she rises and starts to leave]
Where you staying?
With Carrie Duncan.
Crazy Carrie Duncan?
She's not crazy, she just likes the boys.
I'll say.
You should talk. You made out with her at the homecoming game.
I did not. [Liz laughs in disbelief] I didn't not make out with Crazy Carrie Duncan at the homecoming game.
It was really good to see you. And you do look good. [Luke stares at his hands] I will make sure Carrie knows that. [exits]
Wait, wait, wait, wait the tracking says its in Atlanta. What is it doing in Atlanta?
Who is this country that speaks English?
It's America.
Everyday she learns something new.
Okay, Dennis, it is time to get proactive on this.
This is when mild mannered Jason Stiles suddenly darted into a phone booth and ripped off his shirt and became - Proactive Man.
What? I'm sorry I didn't get that last part.
Able to be proactive where ever there is activity of a pro nature.
Dennis, just do this. A messenger is coming in an hour to pick up the box with the checks -- the box with the checks in the drawer by the floor.
The vessel with the pestle holds the brew that is true.
[stares at her in disbelief and suppresses a chuckle] I'm sorry, I'm kind of distracted.
[hisses] Get off the phone!
[muffles the phone] It's the last one, I promise - two minutes tops.
Two minutes and I'm going to throw that thing in the lake.
There's a lake?
We just drove by the lake.
Aw, I missed the lake, can we drive by it again later?
Two minutes! [exasperated, she walks away to the entrance of Kim's Antiques]
Thank you
Hi Mrs. Kim. Hi.
Wow, you've got a lot of new stuff in here. [She watches as Mrs. Kim searches for paperwork in a nearby drawer, then leans closer to speak quietly.] She's fine. She's at Yale with Rory.
Great.
[still on cell phone] No, no, no. I don't see any reason why that can't work out.

[at the entrance - gasps when she sees Jason still on phone] Okay! Ah, I'm sorry but your two minutes are up. Asia, Africa and where ever Jvork is from is just going to have to wait because I'm putting a kibosh on that phone. [Jason waves and gestures wildly to her as she approaches him] I'm sorry mister but I'm clicking that thing off myself.

No, no, no. I am still here, Emily! [Lorelai gasps] There's just a lot of commotion around me. No, I'm not in the office. I took the morning off. Yes, Richard deserves a morning off too. Okay, I'll see you at the hotel. Okay, bye. [clicks phone closed and turns to Lorelai] I pulled a muscle waving at you.
How was I supposed to know you were talking to my mother?
It was a very personal wave. It was a big, broad, over the top personal wave.
She called you?
She called.
[Mock serious tone] Are you doing like a Mrs. Robinson thing with my mother?
[return mock serious tone] Yes. I was visiting Richard one day, and he stepped out and Emily lit a cigarette and did that triangle thing with her thigh.
Well, you said hotel.

Well, she wants me to come to some charity thing at a hotel tomorrow. [Lorelai's cell phone rings and moves to answer] Hey, wait, wait a minute. If I can't be on the phone then you cannot be on the phon..
[she answers the call] Hello?
Lorelai, its me.
Lorelai Gilmore's a hypocrite!
Hello Emily!
Why are you calling me Emily?
'Cause that's your name, ask me again and I tell you the same.
And who was that yelling?
No one you'd know. What's up?
[answers his ringing phone] This is Jason. Oops. [walks away from Lorelai]
That's the same man I heard before. Is he harassing you?
[slowly walks away from Jason's conversation] Ah, err, yes. I'm on the street. Get away you! It's just insanity out here today.
Well, that's not good. Walk down a different street.
I'm turning the corner as we speak. So, what, there's a manuscript thing?
Yes, it's a fund-raiser, and we're stuck and I'm desperate for attendees.
I'll go. Sure. Yes.
Really?
I'll be there. How much - how much do I give?
Nothing. We've already paid.
Okay, why don't you leave the details on where to meet up and all on the home machine.
I will, thank you, and please get out of the street.
I will, bye. [she walks back to where Jason is standing]
Okay, okay, bye. [hangs up] Did she hear me?
Yes, but she thinks you're a raving street loon.
Okay, this is exactly the reason why I hate hiding relationships
I know.
We're gonna get caught.
We can't tell them.
We're gonna get caught.
This is just a freak occurrence.
This is destined to be repeated.
They'll be mad that I hid it.
They'll be madder the longer you hide it.
They'll screw things up, I don't want that. I like us.

But, it's inevitable. They're gonna see us together someplace, or a traffic report will take pictures of cars on the expressway and we'll be sitting in the car - and then Richard will be watching the news and he will see us, so barring some sort of Star Trek-like cloaking device - which was problematic in every incarnation of Star Trek - I remember Kirk complaining about it, I remember Picard complaining about it - they will see us, and we'll get caught.
I'm very uncomfortable dating a Trekkie.

Ah, I-I just don't feel good about this. It makes me very nervous. Listen, I've a very difficult phone call this morning with our Japanese partners and I didn't ever break a sweat, I had that testy call from the client from California - not a drop, but your mother calls and I'm soaked through.
On your morning off too, I'm sorry.
That's okay.
Do you want me to wring your shirt out for you?
No, it's old - and I like us too, by the way which is why I feel so strongly about this.
I know.
I'm not mad.
I know that too. [guiltily shifts her feet]
And I'll do what ever you want, you know them better than I.
I'll tell them.
Really?
Yes. Yes. Tonight's our Friday night dinner. Dad's gone, but starting with Emily might be for the best.
I could talk to Richard, if you want.
Oh no, its my thing. I'll do it.
Good. Oh, look phone is off.
Oh. Good, let's go buy some furniture.
So, you're just sitting here watching TV?

I'm studying. Look at Ted Kennedy, huh? I always admired him as a senator, but you see him and think: It's just so unfair that fat men look good in suits. We girls get a couple of pounds and every piece of fashion betrays…
[clicks off the TV] Off.
What?
I want to talk to you about your boyfriend situation, Paris.
Jamie?
I'm sorry, I should have clarified "boyfriends."
Oh. You mean a certain other fella.
Let's cut the coyness. I want to talk about you having an affair with Professor Asher Fleming and at the same time stringing along poor Jamie, with no concern for his feelings.
It's not an affair.
Affair. Relationship. Fling. Tete-a-tete. What ever you want to call it.
Well, I'm very surprised by this.
How so?
You've never wanted to discuss Asher before.
Well, I don't particularly want to discuss him now, but I'm forced to.
What's forcing you --
I just ran into Jamie, and he's wandering around lonely, missing you, scared of losing you, and you're sitting here watching C-SPAN!
Nobody watches C-SPAN. It's just on in the background.
Well you gotta choose Paris, because this is becoming pretty clear that the what-ever-you-want-to-call-it with the professor is not a short-lived thing.
I'd say that's accurate, and you can just call him Asher.
No, he's my teacher, so I think I'll stick with professor.
Professor just makes him sound old.
He IS old!
He's sixty. Today's sixty is what fifty was twenty years ago and he's got the body of a forty year old.
I really don't want to talk about his body.
I'm not denying that we've got a May-December romance going on here.
This is not May-December, this is May - Ming Dynasty.
An age difference like this is very common. People dating people the same age are passe now.
My grandfather introduced you to him. Do you see how awkward this is for me?
Well, hot men tend to run in packs.
Do not ever say anything like that again.
Mary, you are such a prude.
Well, at least I'm not mean to people who love me. Where is your heart?
I know I've mishandled the Jamie situation. He just can't take a hint.
Well, you gotta do something, because one of us here does care about Jamie and I think its me.
I know. He's my first real boyfriend.
Well, you got lucky with him.
And he's crazy about me, I never quite figured out why.
Oh, don't get so self-deprecating. It's obnoxious.
He's been so forgiving. I've been pretty mean. [picks up cordless phone and starts dialing]
Just talk to him and see how it goes.

[into phone] Hey, it's me. We've got to end this - now. [Rory is shocked.] There's just no reason to prolong it. Sorry you came all the way out here. Well, Rory show me the light. She made me see there's just no point in going on.
Paris!
No, she just came home and we talked. She's right here if you want to ask her, yourself.
Do not give me that phone!
Anyhow, I'm really sorry Jamie. Really. Bye.
That had all the tact of a n*zi storm trooper.
It was your idea.
Breaking up was not my idea.
Well, he'd be stupid if he thought that's why I'd do it. [stands and paces] This was good. It was right. I'm glad I did it. You can have the TV if you want. [exits to bedroom]
Yup, it's that unpredictable time of year, Mrs. Cassini.

Yeah, you too. [He approaches a small locked garage and searches for the key. He notices the lock has been cut. He opens the swinging doors and sees a large wide empty space inside. He expression changes from shock to disappointment.]

[talking on phone] It's a Rambler Ambassador, four door, a rusty brown pretty much a b*at clunker. [pause] No. I don't know how long its been missing. [pause] I mean I saw it for sure last week. Nah, I don't drive it much, it's a second car, okay? [long pause and he sighs] Just, just call me when you find it. Thanks, Bye. [he hangs up]
Oh hey.
Hey.
Tanna just told me that that Chester Fleet guy liked her hair and asked her out. She's throwing up now.
Good for her.
Going somewhere?
Home for the weekend.
Just to get away from me?

No, I've got dinner at my grandma's tonight - obligatory thing - and our town's having its Firelight Festival tomorrow which I haven't missed since I was one, so not seeing you is - Well - quite frankly just a fringe benefit.
Would it make you feel any better to know how awful I feel?
Nope.
I don't understand why you're so upset about this.
I know you don't.
I tried to call Jamie again, he won't pick up.
Can you blame him?

No. I know I let it go too long. I just wasn't sure what Asher was thinking at first. I wasn't sure if it was just a fling for him. But over the past couple of weeks, he's been mentioning stuff about the future. He's spending a month teaching a couple of courses at Oxford over the summer and then he asked me what I was planning to do over the summer. I mean there is a definite implication that he was wondering if I was available during the summer. I think he might ask me to go with him to Oxford. I mean, why else would he ask?
b*at me.
I'm not counting my chickens…
Its good thinking.
But it is the first indication.
Look, I've gotta hit the road.
It was his accent that did it. I'm such the total Anglophile. When I was a kid, I was in love with Neal Kinnock.
Who?
The former head of the Labour party. Teeth like a horse, but oh that voice, and then there was Roger Moore -
English accents are nice.
He TiVos Frontline.
Who does?
Asher. So we can watch it together.
Terrific.
You don't think he meant we'd be together this summer?
I wasn't there.
I'm not counting my chickens.
I think that's smart. [starts to leave]

I never wanted to hurt Jamie. I just don't know how to do these things. I'm not very nice sometimes. I hope Asher doesn't see that in me. [long pause] I didn't mean to hold you up. Have a good weekend.
[pauses at the door] I just want you to be happy. You know that, right?
[smiles for the first time] Thanks. I'm happy.
[calls out over the blare of the music before turning volume down] Mom? Hello?
[comes down stairs] Oh, Rory. Good. I did not go suddenly half deaf. Were you supposed to meet me here?
No, I'm a surprise.
As was your conception.
I'll just be two minutes. [exits to go to her room to change]
As was your conception.
[call off camera] Hey, how was your day with Jason?
Fun! He makes me laugh.
Aww, I like that
[calls out so Rory can hear] He's very off-center. It's been a while since I've been with someone off-center.
Cool.
I'm telling Mom tonight - about us.
I think Grandma knows you're my mother.
About me and Jason.
Very brave.
Yeah. [she joins Rory and they walk through the kitchen] Jason's wanted to from the beginning. It's the mature thing to do and that's why I didn't want to do it, but it's time.
That's weird [looking in kitchen cabinet]
What's weird?
This. [takes out loaf of bread]
Bread? Bread is weird?
It's weird when its here. It does not make a good snack.
It does when you add stuff to it, like cheese.
We have cheese? [moves to the refrigerator and opens]
Yeah. It's not "Donner Pass", we have cheese.
Whoa! It's like a frickin' cornucopia.
Yeah, there's the stuff.
There's the cheese!
Yeah, yeah. Why are you making such a big deal about this?
Because we never had real food in this house the whole time I was growing up.
What? We always had food. This fridge was never empty.
Well, yeah. We had left overs from take-out - cold pizza, Luke's fries, but never stuff you had to assemble.
Okay chill out on the inquiry. [pushes door closed]
Is that a cucumber?
Listen, you'd make a terrible private investigator, because you get hung up on all sorts of dumb stuff that does not matter - now come on. We're late, I'll drive. [leads her out the kitchen door]
Sounds good. [points to the basket on the stove] Oh my God, is that a tomato?
Enough already. Let's go.
Ah, my girls are arriving together.
Hi, Mom.
Hi, Grandma.
You smell like coffee. [assists the maid with their coats]
We haven't had any.
It's so strong.
Okay, Mom. I really don't like you sniffing me.
Hey where's Grandpa tonight?

He's in Manhattan having dinner with clients. He just called. They're at some restaurant near Times Square. He said that Times Square just keeps getting cleaner and cleaner. They didn't stumble upon one prostitute the whole night.
Oh yeah. I heard the Disney Company had them all k*ll.
What I don't understand is why Jason wouldn't make this trip instead.
Oh. Well, he's maybe busy with his own thing.
I know for a fact he wasn't. Richard said he took the whole morning off.
Well, everyone deserves an occasional morning off.
Richard never takes a morning off. He's up every day at five-thirty on the phone then it's out the door to the office. I bet Jason doesn't roll out of bed until eight.
On the contrary - he - probably gets up earlier than eight. You know, I would think that he would have to, to keep up with Dad.
[frowning] Makes sense.
[uncomfortable] Just a guess.
I just find that boy so irritating. He's always trying to get in good with me. Complimenting me, agreeing with me. He's absolutely prostrating himself at my feet. It's so weak.
Well you're a formidable opponent, Mom. They don't call you the Edie Amine of the DAR for nothing.
He's so grating about it. I'm never fully comfortable around him.
Well you should maybe try harder.
I try. But every time I see him a new facet of his Jason-ish comes out.
It's good to have different facets, and there's probably a lot you don't know about him.
Oh, I'm sure about that. You two would be perfect for each other.
What? Who, me and Jason?
A match made in heaven.
Well, thanks a lot!
Don't get upset. [rises to go make drinks]

Well Mom, you just spent the last five minutes listing every off-putting quality Jason has, real or imagined and then you put me on his level and you say we're perfect together. [Emily begins laughing at the bar table] What's so funny?
I'm sorry - [continues to laugh]
Did I miss something? Did a clown come in behind me and start doing funny pratfalls, what?
Just the idea of you and Jason together, it's funny.
[to a grinning Rory] It's funny.
It's really funny. I just said it as a joke.
You said it as a joke.
You took it so seriously.
But why is it so funny?
Well, think about it.
I am. I just trying to figure out what you're thinking.
Well, it's obvious.
It's not obvious to me or to Rory. Rory's wondering, aren't you?
Yeah, why is that so funny, Grandma?
It would just be so ludicrous.
But why, because he's a - you know, he's a hard-working guy from what I know.
[continues to laugh harder] I'm sorry, you're making me laugh even harder about it. I just said it off hand.
I know.
[offers drink to Lorelai] Martini?
You didn't have to shake it much with all that laughing, you know, the laughing just shook it on up for ya.
It's good to laugh like that once in a while.
Oh yeah. I know.
You okay? [Lorelai doesn't respond] You didn't tell her. Next time? How are your motor k*ll? I'll drive. [She takes the keys from her mother]
Luke.
Oh, Hey Coop.
Good news, found the car.
Oh good. Who would steal that thing. It's just a hunk of junk.
It broke down on the expressway a couple of hours ago, the guy was in it.
You got the guy?
Yeah, but there's not a lot we can do, the guy's the owner.
What do you mean? I'm the owner.
Well, not according to the registration. It's registered to a --
Jess Mariano. [watches the tow truck drive by]

Yep. Says you're his uncle. Registration's long expired, too. It needs seeing to. But I just figured that since these seems like a family matter, I'd bring the car and the kid back to you. [Luke watches Jess step out of the police cruiser.]
Yeah, a family matter.
Where do you want it?
Right there's fine.
This isn't wasn't my idea.
You'll take care of the registration?
Yeah, thanks Coop.
[sarcastic] Yeah, thanks Coop.
[to his partner] Lets go, Frank.
Well, look who's back.
I'm only here to retrieve my property.
[crossed arms] You've got a lot of nerve.
You've got a lot of nerve.
How so? [squad car drives away as they talk]
You stole my car. Coop should have arrested you, why didn't he arrest you?
Free donuts.
Beautiful.
So you got anything you wanna say?
You could have washed it once in a while?
Okay fine, the car is yours, our business here is done, hasta la vista, have a nice life. [starts to leave]
Our business here is not done. My car is wrecked because of you.
Oh yeah?

Three of the tires are leaking, its got no oil, the floats in the carburetor are probably cracked so it's back-firing like mad, I mean, people were ducking when I was driving by. Then it stalled and wouldn't start.
Well, you can find Mr. Goodwrench in the Yellow Pages, I think it's under M or is it G? I can never tell with those kinds of things.
You're paying for the repairs.
Oh, don't make me laugh.
It's broken because of you.
That thing was a piece of junk to begin with, the paint is the only thing holding it together.
And the expired registration? I'm gonna have to pay a fine.
So, I guess it didn't work out with your dad, huh?
It worked out fine.
So, what are you doing back East, buddy? Still searching?
Been traveling.
Well, thanks for all the swell cards and letters you sent while you were away.
You kicked me out, what were you expecting - a candygram?
I didn't kick you out, you got yourself kicked out.
Nice spin, you should work for Bush.
So what did you get out of this Kerouac trip of yours? You write the great American novel or something? You learn how to play the harmonica?
What do you care, you're not my guardian anymore.
And I bless every day that I'm not.
Well, when you're not good at something, it's best to cut and run.
Aww, I'm sorry I tried to give you a decent life, Jess. I'm sorry I didn't think driving a fork-lift for the rest of your life was good enough for you.
Oh that is condescending, isn't it? I thought you were a friend of the working man.
Oh, that sister of mine, what a prize. What a prize.
What does she have to do with any of this?
I tell her about the car, she runs and tells you. That's what happened, right? Her claiming she had no contact.
Again, the car is mine. Liz was doing the right thing, that's what family does.
Family? What a joke coming from you.
Go clean your counters, I'm tired.
So, you staying in town?
I don't know of any twenty-four hour auto shops around here, do you?
Well, you're not staying with me.
It didn't cross my mind.
Get it fixed quick.
Believe me, no one wants it fixed faster than me.
You stay away from her while you're here.
Stay away from who?
You know who I mean.
Gee, you're so cryptic.
You've done all the damage there you're gonna, okay?
I'm here to get my car, then I'm gone. [walks away from Luke toward his stranded car]
Where are you staying?
Backseat's as comfy as anywhere.
Fine. [As Jess gets in his chilly car, Luke returns to his diner]
Please do not say that word again.
It's a free country.
Just say hot chocolate or say nothing at all.
Mmm, terrific "Ho-Cho".
Oooh, I hate that. It's so cutsey-wootsey.
Do you hate it as much as my favorite summer treat?
Don't!
An ice-cold Fro-Yo! [takes out her cell phone]
Stop! Just stop - who are you calling?
I'm calling Jason, I promised I would check in. [cell phone rings] Hello.
I'm dying here, how'd it go?
Weeeell, it didn't.
[disappointed sigh] Oh.
Sorry.
Na - it's a long story - the timing was very bad. [Rory stands shivering]
No, no. I - ah, yeah - kind of. [Rory and Lorelai continue to walk down the sidewalk]
Lorelai, we've got to do it.
Well, the timing has to be right
It's going to be awkward no matter when you do it.
Not if they're both unconscious.
Yeah, but then you're going to be dealing with why both your parents are unconscious, and doctors consultations, and phoning friends and relatives - the timing is bad there too.

Listen, it's ah - trust me, this was not good timing, and I swear to you there'll be much better timing in the near future. [their stroll takes them to the front of Luke's diner where they stop. Rory notices a familiar car parked across the street. She slowly walks toward it.] Well, near is near - I can't define it more than that. Uh, it's closer than far, how's that?
[She stands close enough to see Jess asleep in the backseat.] I don't believe this.
[concerned] Uh, honey - I gotta call you back, okay? Bye. Um, is that - ?
Yes.
Oh.
I don't believe this.
What is he doing here?
What is he doing - there? [indicating the car]
Asleep in his car - is he living in it?
I don't see stuff.
Does Luke know he's here?
Well, I know what you know.
[disbelief] He - may not know.
Well, it's right in front of his place. How could he not know?
Well, it's freezing out here. He could die, he must not know.
Or doesn't care.
Do you think David Blain put him up to this?
Why is he here? I mean, why did he come back?
Light's still on in there, Luke's in there somewhere - should we go talk to him?
[uncomfortable] No. It's too weird. [shivers] And it's - weird.
Definitely weird.
Well, I'll just see you at home. I'm - cause I don't want to deal with this. I'll see you at home. [She quickly walks off, while Lorelai pauses a moment before walking to Luke's diner door.]
Hey, come on in.
Are you aware of whose out there?
Yeah, I'm aware [continues to stack chairs on tables]
That he's sleeping in his car?
Yeah.
It's about thirty-five degrees.
He's a tough guy, he can take it.
Luke, why is he back here?
Because I'm stupid.
Meaning?
Well his mom showed up -- for what reason I don't know -- I'm still waiting for that shoe to drop. I mention Jess' car and then - boom - there's Jess.
So the mystery woman from this morning? That's Liz?
In all her glory
Quite a day you've had.

Oh, it's been delightful. I think Bobby McFerrin's gonna write one of those happy boop-boopdy-doo songs of his about this. I mean, she lied to me about having contact with Jess, so she's lied about everything else.
But why is he sleeping in his car?
Because he's going to wait to have it fixed, it's a point of pride with the little punk. But please, don't tell Rory, he'll be gone tomorrow, no reason to upset her.
Well, she's already seen him.
[grimacing] Oh man!
She's fine Luke. She's over it.
Well, he won't go near her, I'll make sure of that.
Again, I don't think it's necessary. She can fend for herself.
[exasperated] What a lie it all is!
All what is?

Families. I mean, they're just messes. It's like this - spilled drink that just keeps spilling, and ya gotta keep cleaning it up, and you scrub and you scrub and you just can't get the stain up! Show me a happy family - just one. Didn't that Tolstoy-guy say something about families?
Probably
It's a famous thing he said. It's like: "all families are unhappy" …or, or, or "happy on the surface"… or "unhappy in the same way"…
Sounds a little incomplete.
Well, y'know, maybe he couldn't complete the thought because he was dealing with his stinkin' family.
Do the Hallmark people know about you? 'Cause you're a natural.
(throws his hands up helplessly) I'm tired of cleaning up messes. I'm tired of helping people who do nothing to help themselves!
I'm sorry you're so upset. I just don't want you to have to deal with the frozen carcass in the morning
He'll be fine.
Okay. Try to get some rest, okay? Relax. Watch a little TV - no family shows…
(chuckles) Yeah, yeah… I'm going up now.
Bye. [she leaves and Luke, obviously upset, watches after her]
Hey.
Hey. So, do you want an update?
I guess.
Well, the whole thing - the mystery woman from this morning? Jess' mom.
Whoa.
Still a mystery though. Luke's not quite sure what she's up to.
She came with Jess?
She called him or something. It's very confusing. Luke was not in an expansive story telling mood. All he knows is that Jess said he came for his car and he's not leaving without it.
Okay.
Yeah. Which means he might be here part of the day tomorrow, so uh, "Danger, Will Robinson."
I can live with it, really.
That's what I told Luke.
Good.
Okay. So, I'm going to go upstairs, get warm - Good night.
Hey, um, before you go.
Hmm?
What happened to our movie channels?
What do you mean?
Well, I was flipping through cable and a bunch of our channels are gone.
Oh. Well, that's not right.
And you have bread.
[chuckles] There's a connection?
Are you skimping?
What?
Cutting back on things, cable, eating out, the bread, the cheese, the tomato
Okay, hey - if you're going to try me in a court of law, the bread, the tomato and I will need to hire a lawyer.
There's no takeout in the fridge, no takeout containers in the trash.
You're going through the trash?
And I'm not seeing the stacks of magazines lying around. We always subscribe to everything.
Yes, we do. I've read them all, they're in recycle bin - you can go check.
It even seems a little darker in here - like you're using a lower watt bulb, or something.
Oh my God, you're reading into everything.
You're not having money problems?
No. I mean, I'm not going to be on the Fortune 500 list anytime soon, but I'm fine.
With the Inn and everything?
Yes. We're getting a horse.
Cool. And food for the horse?
He'll be well fed.
Just as long as you're well fed too.
Yeah, I'll call the cable company in the morning. I think we should be getting those channels.
Well, you'd tell me, right?
Yes.
[closes her study folder and kisses Lorelai's cheek] Well, goodnight.
Good night angel. [Rory rises and leaves. When she is out of sight, Lorelai clicks off the nearby table lamp.]
[muffled inside as Luke continues pounding on the glass] Go away. [Eventually Jess impatiently rises and rolls down the window.] What?
I'm spending the night with Nicole.
Thanks for the update.

The hidden key is still in the same place. Now, you can stay out here and freeze to death if you want or you can go inside, I don't really give a damn, it makes no difference to me. [walks off without waiting for an answer]
Fine. [rolls his window up]
Cold, cold, cold, cold ! Icy feet, stupid frozen-tundra house! Oh. [She picks up a shawl and wraps herself in it. She sees someone sleeping on the couch, bundled in blankets.]

Honey, why are you sleeping in here? Your room is way warmer. [She turns up the thermostat and goes into the kitchen.] Okay, here's the question for today, kids. What the hell are the Eskimos thinking? I mean, yes, the hoods are cute, but it's always cold. Always! Plus you have to eat fish for breakfast and you have to eat whales and then polar bears and penguins and Santa Claus... [Comes back from the kitchen, towards the couch and sits on the sleeping figure] Okay, coffee's on, Pop-Tarts are pop-tarting! If you're just going to lie there, I'm going to have to sit here. I'm going to make myself very comfortable on a nice, warm Rory!
Why is it so cold in here?
Ahh!
Ahh!
I thought I was sitting on you!
Oh, really? Good trick...
Well, if you are there, then who is this?
I don't know.
We've got a stranger in our house.
Robert Downey, Jr?
Or a m*rder.
... who needed to take a nap before committing his crimes?
I think this belongs to you.
She must have followed me home from Yale. I told her she could hang out there this weekend.
But why do that when you can come here and sleep where penguins need a coat?
Yeah, why is it so cold in here?
I broke that stupid window trying to lock it last night.
Well, get it fixed, woman.
I left Luke a message just now. He'll do it.
Before or after the re-enactment of Alive?
Hopefully before.
Why don't you call a guy?
What guy?
A window fixing guy.

Ah, Luke always gets mad when I pay someone to do something that he could do for free. And then he lectures me about it every time I see him and it's annoying. "Oh, you paid him how much to fix the window? What, you couldn't just find someone to steal your purse that day? Hey, while you're at it I've got an idea, why don't you go down to a Versateller and let them charge you five bucks to take your own money out of the bank? Or buy some tickets at Ticketmaster and wind up paying more in service charges than it would cost you to see the band? Oh, here's a great fifty buck mark up on a bottle of wine that it would have cost you ten dollars in the supermarket you're missing!"
Oh my God, Luke is annoying.
So…
What?
Just wondering what you're thinking about.
I'm thinking about nothing.
Nothing wouldn't happen to wear a leather jacket and be able to pull off an extremely convincing "Adrian!" would it?
No, it wouldn't. You think he froze to death?
No, He wasn't sleeping here.
Right.
I'm sure Luke took care of it.
Hey, did somebody sit on me just now?
No, why?
My hip hurts.
Oh, getting old...
Hey, did anyone ever think that maybe Sylvia Plath wasn't crazy, she was just cold?
I'm supposed to say roger, Kirk.
I don't think so. Copy. Roger.
Roger means I heard you, Kirk. I was supposed to say roger.
Negative. I am in charge here and I say roger! ROGER.
No, you don't.
If he says roger, what the hell am I supposed to say?
Who cares?
Get out of the way, Kirk.
Hold on. Roger.
This car is not stopping.
I am planning the Firelight Festival. Taylor left me in charge, and I have to make sure everything is perfect.
MOVE!
Roger.
Go away.
The Budweiser Clydesdales prancing along, Ann Jillian waving in the back.
I've got to get my car to Gypsy so she can fix it and I can leave.
So you decided to push it there.
I didn't have a choice.
I'm going as fast as I can, jerk!
Jess, do you at all find this ridiculous?
Why, yes, as a matter of fact, I do find this ridiculous. I find it ridiculous that Gypsy won't walk twenty feet to take a look at my car.
Hire a tow truck.
It costs eighty bucks to hire a tow truck. Oh, come on, it's like freakin' Carnivale out here.
I'll give you the eighty bucks.
No.
You're blocking the whole street.
I don't want your money.
You wanna get out of here, let me pay the eighty bucks.
Hey, how about more walkie, and less talkie.
You're making a spectacle of yourself.
Go home, you won't have to watch.
Fine.
Well?
Still looking.
What's the matter with it?
Still looking.
You've been circling around the thing for fifteen minutes. You waiting for it to tell you where it hurts?
I've seen dumber things talk.
Just tell me what's wrong with the car.
You need a carburetor.
So how long until it's fixed?
Not sure.
It has to be today. I have to walk out of this half-mile, four-block, freakhole of a medical experiment.
You are delightful. I'll have you out of here tonight. Go away and come back at closing.
Fine.
And bring a lot of money because I'm going to overcharge you like you've never been overcharged before.
I'll bet you say that to all the guys.
On second thought, maybe I'm closing early tonight.
I'm going.
That's not her.
What?
She cut her hair.
Don't know what you're talking about.
Okay, my mistake.
Okay, now. Hold it. Oh, okay, how does it look?
Festive and femme.
Yes, and completely ineffective.
Maybe it just needs another layer.
Yes, of glass.
Nice. Something to protect us from freezer burn.
Come over here and help us.
I'm not going to help you Barbie Band-aid our window. I will, however, help you to call one of the many extremely qualified window repairmen that I've circled for you in the phone book.
Hey, if we fix the window before Luke comes over, he will have his feelings hurt. Do you want that?
Phone book's on the kitchen table.
Where are you going?
I'm going to take a walk, get a Danish, hit the bookstore, and I'll be back for lunch.
Okay.
[to Lane] Maybe if we add a layer of tinfoil.
Hey, professional window guys are driving by, pointing and laughing. I just thought you should know.
Thank you.
So, listen, I have some errands to run today. Do you need anything?
No, I'm fine.
Okay. I'll probably be heading down Elm.
Well, that's a good street.
Yes, it is. If there is anything you'd want me to do on Elm, or anyone you wanted me to see, I could...
That's okay. Has she said anything to you?
No, but she's wanted to.
How can you tell?
Let's just say it's a mom thing.
Yeah, well...
Okay, well maybe tomorrow then.
Hello?
It's a complete disaster!
My existence?
Not everything is about you, Lorelai.
Oh, sorry.
The rare manuscripts acquisition fundraiser is tonight and we still haven't filled our table. I'm four people short.
The Burles are going to visit their daughter in New Hampshire.
Well then they can just go straight to hell, then, can't they?
Mom, I already said I'd go.
But we still have a half empty table.
Well, fewer people to fight over the centerpiece.
Stop it. This is not funny. The last person who didn't fill her table was Loretta Bobbins. Do you remember Loretta Bobbins?
No.
Exactly! Once you do not fill your table, you do not get another table to fill. You are off the list.
Mom, that's not gonna happen to you.
You said you would come.
I am coming.
And you're bringing someone.
I never said I was bringing someone.
Well, I'm telling you to now.
Mom, it's tonight.
I need you to bring someone, Lorelai.
But I…
Loretta Bobbins, Lorelai.
All right, the Dartmores are trying to change Bitty's viewing. They'll call back in a minute.
They owe us, Richard. Remind them that they owe us.
All right. I'll see you tonight at six o'clock sharp and don't wear those pantyhose with the seams up the back. You look like ten cents a dance.
Richard, I need a gimlet.
After we light the bonfire, the dancers should come through.
Okay, Kirk.
They'll circle the gazebo. Jazz hands, jazz hands, jazz hands. Then out come the flaming batons.
That sounds good, Kirk.
Are you ignoring me?
Since you were old enough to walk, Kirk.
What do you think?
I think it's good.
Is there too much turquoise?
Are you kidding? Turquoise is timeless.
What are you doing?
Oh, hey, Luke. You remember my friend Carrie, right?
Oh, yeah. Hey, Carrie.
Hi, Butch, good to see you. Been under any bleachers lately?
No, I haven't. What is that?
It's an earring tree.
And what is it for?
You hang earrings on it.
And what is it doing here?
I thought I'd put some of my earrings out, you know, and see if I could sell some to the good people of Stars Hollow.
No.
Why?
They're cute.
This is a diner. People come here to eat, not shop.
But now they can do both.
Uh-huh. Hey, Liz, can I talk to you for a moment?
Hey, Liz, you want me to negotiate with him for you?
No, she doesn't, Carrie. Thanks for the offer. Liz, please?
Sure, my brother.
Why are you so stressed about this?
Liz, do you remember when you decided to make those ceramic pots?
Yes.
Without a kiln?
Yes.
And how did that go?
Pretty bad.
You were depressed for a month, you cut all your hair, you threw out all your clothes...
I remember the bad times.
You put those earring out on my counter and nobody buys them…
They sell great at the fairs.
I'm sure they do, but this is not a renaissance fair. Look around. Everybody here has a life. No one's gonna buy them. Please, just--
Oh, look at this. Oh, these are so cute! Luke, are you selling these?
He sure is.
Well, I'll take 'em.
Excuse me, I wanted those.
Turquoise? With your complexion?
They're for Lulu. She's a sweetheart.
Does she have pierced ears?
Um, I can check. [Speaks into the walkie-talkie.] Joe, have you ever noticed my girlfriend's lobes?
Okay, thank you both for the show of support. It's very kind but you don't have to do this.
Do what?
Pretend that you like them because Liz made them.
Who's pretending?
Yeah, they're phat.
They're gonna fall apart.
No they're not.
They're gonna make people's ears green and send them to the hospital.
You cannot design my ad campaign.
Liz!
You need to nap, Jack. I'm cool, they're cool, everybody's cool.
Stop, Kirk!
Ouch! She slapped me! Who saw her slap me?
Okay, relax you two. I can make you whatever you want!
I want these ones in fuchsia pink. I want these in purple...
Hi, I'd like a large coffee and a cherry Danish, please.
I'm leaving.
A little farther back. Roger.
What?
It's gotta go back farther. Roger.
I can't hear you.
Speak into to your walkie-talkie. Roger.
Kirk, what are you saying?
[into the walkie-talkie.] Speak into your... [Gives up and yells] Speak into your walkie-talkie! Roger!
I lost my walkie-talkie. I told you that.
Well, then it's your own fault! Roger!

Hey, Luke, hey Luke, hold on! Please, I know you owe us nothing but our dead frozen carcasses may someday haunt you in your old age, or not... because… [She sees Liz on the driver's seat.] you don't know who I am. Hi. Sorry. I thought you were Luke.
I should put on some lipstick.
No, I just saw the truck.
Well, I borrowed the truck.
Right.
He knows.
I'm sure he does.
I'm Liz, Luke's sister.
Oh, Luke's sister, yeah, I knew you were here. Hi, I'm Lorelai. So, is Luke in the diner?
No, he just stepped out for a sec. You need him for something?
I just needed to tell him something, I ...
You want me to give him a message?
Sure, yeah, um, tell him Lorelai wanted to gently remind him about the window. I'll be home until five-thirty and tell him I looked cold.
Oh, you're the wife.
The wife?
Yeah, I knew he got married, but I hadn't seen the face yet. So, oh wow, it's good to meet you.
No, no, no. I'm not the wife. I'm the friend and the customer, not the wife.
Oh, sorry. You look like his type, so…
No, no, not his type or his wife, just his friend. And his customer.
Well, still good to meet you.
You too. Luke has told me a lot about you.
Yeah, like what?
Oh, like you're his sister…
He admits it!
And that, you know, you're here visiting him, and how happy he is that you're visiting him.
He did not say that.
I think he did.
He's not probably too thrilled I'm here. I'm kind of pain in his ass.
Well, aren't we all?
Yeah, but I'm special. I kinda screw up a lot and then he has to fix it and then we fight and then I screw up again and he fixes it - it's a pattern.
Well, Luke likes his routine.

He's pretty amazing though. No matter how much I screw up, he just keeps fixing it. I need money, he gives me money. No place to live, Luke finds an apartment. Even my kid when I was having trouble with him -- did you ever meet Jess?
Oh yes, I did.
I tell you, he was hell on wheels. I couldn't do a thing with him. I didn't know what to do, so...
Luke fixed it?

He tried. He wasn't entirely successful. I don't know, maybe if I had sent Jess to him a little sooner… Well, anyhow, Luke did what he could. He always does. He's like my hero, you know. Like one of those Greek gods with the golden helmets and the shields and the sandals.
And the little white toga dresses.
I sound silly.
No, you don't. Take it from someone who's run to Luke many a time. He's definitely one of the good ones. Maybe THE good one.
Yeah, I miss him. I've even been thinking of moving back here.
To Stars Hollow?
Maybe. I've discussed it with my boyfriend. I'm not sure how Luke would like it, but I sure would. Well, I should get going.
Sure.
Well, it was nice to meet you, friend and customer, not wife.
Nice to meet you too.
I'll be sure and give him your message.
Don't forget, human popsicle.
Well, I have to tell you this is a real treat having you two girls over, like spur of the moment, I don't know what I did to get so damned lucky.
Well, we just realized we hadn't seen you very much lately and we thought "Hey, today is the perfect day to catch up with Babette."
Oh, yeah, the perfect day.
Well I am tickled pink. Here you go-- hot cocoa.
Thanks, Babette.
Ahh, we don't deserve such treatment.
Of course you do -- two young hotsy-totsies like yourselves hanging out with an old bird like me. You deserve a lot better. So, you kids going to the Firelight Festival tonight?
You bet.
We're going to be late though because we have to make a pit stop at one of my mother's charity events.
Ooh, sounds ritzy.
Like the cracker.

Well, the festival should be quite a shindig. Just watching Kirk trying to get those stars hung was worth the price of admission. You know, he insisted on demonstrating the correct way to hang 'em and treed himself. It took the fire department and two cans of tuna to get him down.
I hate that I missed that.

Plus, the whole town is buzzing about Jess coming back. Stupid little pisher, trying to sneak out of town without anyone knowing. This town, what is he kidding? Oh, I'm so sorry, sugar. Here I am, going on and on about Jess.
It's fine, Babette. I'm fine.
She's fine.
You sure?
Yes. I'm sure.
She's fine.
I saw him.
Who?
Jess?
Yes.
When?
Where?
Today at Weston's.
He went into Weston's?
That little bastard.
What happened?
I went in, he saw me and he left.
No!
He said nothing?
No, he said something. He said, "I'm leaving."
Way to state the obvious.
It was so weird. I mean, he's the one who left town. He's the one who didn't call and now he just gets up and walks out like he's mad.
What does he have to be mad about?
Exactly! I should be mad. It's my town. I should be the one to walk out in a huff.
You still stuck on him, honey?
No, I'm not. I just wasn't expecting him to come back, that's all.
He'll be gone soon.
Yeah, I know. He'll be gone soon.
Oh my God, I forgot the marshmallows!
He'll be gone soon.
Mayday! Mayday! The Morrison kids have stolen the bonfire again! I repeat: the kids have stolen the bonfire again!
Cesar, I'm back. What did you burn? Liz!
Luke, hi!
What are you doing?
I just needed some things.
Steaks?
Yeah.
You needed steaks?
Well, I'm making dinner upstairs and you don't have anything.
Then go to a store.
Oh, come on, a couple of steaks. What's the big deal?
The big deal is, I run a diner. I sell food, that's how I make my living. It's how I can afford all this.
Oh, you can spare a couple of things.
How do you know what I can spare? That's a whole pie.
It's a peach pie. Nobody eats the peach.
A lot of people eat the peach.
I'll buy a pie tomorrow. Tonight I'm making a feast for my guys.
Your guys? Who are your guys?
You and T.J.
T. J.?
Yep, you're really gonna like him. He's upstairs right now waiting for us and he--
Upstairs in my apartment? You left some guy named T.J. alone in my apartment? Ah, Liz!
I've been gone twenty seconds.
That's all it takes.
To do what? Steal the singing "Be Happy" Bass?
Hey, that is my singing "Be Happy" Bass and it had better still be up there, including the batteries.
Hey, I thought I'd make chili. [T.J. turns around and sees Luke.] You are not Liz.
Already smarter than the last guy.
Hi, baby. Look what I found downstairs.
You must be Luke.
I think she's talking about the steaks.
I was not talking about the steaks. This is my "Him." This is my guy. This is T.J.
Guess what it stands for?
What?
T.J. Guess what it stands for?
I don't know.
Just guess.
I can't.
Come on.
Thomas Jefferson?
No. Thomas Jefferson? Wowl, that's a weird guess.
Okay, you know, I've gotta go back.
Oh no, come on, Cesar's there, sit down.
You want a beer?
You mean one of my beers out of my fridge? Sure, why not.
Coming right up.
Oh, I'm so excited. My two favorite guys are here with me, drinking, talking…
And soon, there will be chili.
I forgot something.

Oh my God, this is freaky. It's like fate. Jess didn't know we were here. I had no idea that Jess would come by and now look at us together. All the men in my life are drawn here to me. This is positive. This means something. Do you feel it?
I sure do.
Baby, this is my kid. This is Jess. Jess, this is T.J.
Guess what it stands for.
No.
Oh, you'll stay for dinner.
I've gotta go check on my car.
Come on, we're making a ton of food. There's beer.
My beer.
I'm not hungry.
Oh please, stay for a little while. I think you guys are really gonna get along great.
Oh, T.J. is really enjoying Stars Hollow. Aren't you, baby?
Oh yeah, this place is great. It reminds me of New York.
How?
You know.
Neither one is in space.
No, that's not it.
Of course not.
There's an energy, right?
There is. I feel it. A very similar energy.
Liz showed me your old house and your school. Like the picture of you in the shorts.
My brother was very big in athletics in his day. And the ladies loved him. Ask Carrie. They went out.
Crazy Carrie and I did not go out.
They just made out.
We did not make out. We did not go out. We did nothing that involved the word out.
I think he's still hung up on her.
A lightening bolt, please.
I gotta go.
Oh, okay, but come back after you've checked your car. We'll save you some food. You look good. Handsome.
If I was some girl, I wouldn't kick him out of bed.
Come back, okay?
Okay.
Yeah, if you do, I'll draw your portrait on my Etch-A-Sketch.
Hey, can't miss that.
We'll see.
Hey, Jess wait a sec.
So, wow.
Yep.
Well, if I had to pick anyone in the world for my sister to be with, that guy would definitely be his cab driver.
I don't know. He had a certain something.
Yeah, lack of chromosomes.
That sounds right.
So, what do we do?
About what?
About that, them, him.
Nothing.
Where are you going?
To check on my car.
But Jess, don't you think that we should discuss this?
Discuss what?
T.J.
I thought we just did.
But we didn't come up with a solution.
A solution to what?
Are we having the same conversation? A solution to him.
A solution would have been birth control. Too late, move on.
Jess, we have to do something about this.
Like what?
I don't know. We have to say something.
Like what?
He's a grown man with an Etch-A-Sketch!
So shake him real hard. Maybe he'll disappear.
Oh come on. What, do you like this guy?
Of course I don't like this guy. I don't like any of the guys, but she's gonna do what she's gonna do.
No, I do not accept that. We can go to Liz together. We can tell her--
She does not care what we think. She really doesn't care what I think. I've got nineteen years of proof to back me up.
Yes, she does. You just have to find the right angle with Liz.
Can I go please?
No, you can't go. We have to fix this. I cannot watch her throw her life away again with a loser again.

You see, this is your problem. You're going to help people whether they want it or not. You have to fix everything. You have to fix everyone. You think it makes you a good guy, but really, it just makes you a pain in the ass. You make it so that when people fail you, you get to feel like the martyr and they get to feel like not only did they screw up, but they also disappointed you. You interfere and you make everything worse. No one is asking for your help. No one wants your help. Focus on your own life and leave everyone else alone.
Give it back! Give it back! I mean it! I'm in charge here guys! Come on! Give it back! I need that!
Hey, Andrew. Can you track these down for me? They're all out of print.
You got it.
Thanks.
Ow! Damn it.
Hello?
Oh, Luke.
Oh yeah. Hey.
How did you get in here?
You left your bedroom window open.
My bedroom window is on the second floor. What did you do?
Well, I promised to fix your window, so I'm here to fix your window.
Oh, my God, you cut yourself.
Glass was broken.
Hence the need for fixing. I'm sorry. Are you drunk?
I am not drunk. I do not get drunk.
Huh.
I had some beer-beers. More than one. A few. And then I came here and I climbed your tree.
Well, good thinking.
And then I fell out of your tree.
Hm, sit down.
I landed flat on my back. I felt like Kirk.
Hold your hand up in the air.
And then I climbed back up the tree. This time I made it. I got in. Sorry about the lamp.
You know, Luke, you could have broken your neck.
You know, it would have been all right if I had. I would have fixed it because that's what I do: I fix things. Even when they don't want to be fixed.
Let me see your hand.
Why?
Because it is bleeding and I need to look at it. [Luke shows her his hand.] Ew! Gross!
It's fine, leave it.
I can't leave it, it's cut.
That's my wrist.
Ah, sorry.
You're very good at this.
I don't like blood okay?
So leave it alone.
No, I can't leave it. [Lorelai puts a Band-aid on the cut.] Do you want to tell me what happened?
Nothing.
What are you doing?
I'm going to fix the window.
Forget the window.
I can't forget the window. I made a promise and I'm the reliable guy who helps everybody out whether they like it or not.
What?

Oh, yeah. Nothing I can do about it, just the way I am. It is my big problem. Didn't know it was my big problem until today, but now I know. It is my big problem. [Luke looks at his hand] Got a handful of Barbie.
Luke, what happened today?
Today I found out what a big, dumb, idiot guy I am. Just an imposing, judgmental know-it-all who blows around yelling and complaining and screwing up everybody else's life.
I hardly think you're--
I'm dumb. Yeah, not like Jess. Jess is smart. You know, he doesn't care about anybody else's life. He just takes care of himself.
Did you and Jess have a thing?
He informed me that I am nothing but an unwelcome burden to everyone around me.
Luke, that's not true.
Yes, it is.
Luke, stop it. Liz was just saying today how grateful she is to have you as her brother and how much she looks up to you.
You talked to Liz?
I thought she was you.
I'm a man.
Well, she was in your truck.
When I'm in my truck, I'm still a man.
I couldn't see who was driving, okay? I went over the truck and we met and we started talking.
You shouldn't have talked to Liz.
She worships you. She said she even wants to move to Stars Hollow so she can be closer to you.
She didn't say that.
She did say that. Jess is an unhappy kid, Luke. He's angry. He doesn't mean the things he says.
He did me a favor.
Listen, why don't you hang out here and rest for little while, okay? We'll get you a real bandage.
I like the Barbie ones.
Yes, honey, but the other kids will b*at you up if they see you with one of those. I'll be right back.
Hm.
You sure I can't help you? Can I hand you something? You know, it doesn't have to be perfect, it just has to run.
Just curious--have you noticed since you started standing there, there's been a lot less of the clinking sounds? And the clinking sounds are the sounds tools make when they fix things.
You've been fixing this car for hours.
And I'm not done, so, back off.
Jess!
Hey, she sounds mad.
You've been here less than twenty-four hours and already I wanna k*ll you.
What did I do to you?
All the crap you said to Luke--
What crap?
A man who has done nothing but support you and try to help you.
I don't know what you're talking about.
You do know what I'm talking about. Don't act stupid. Why would you do that? What an incredibly insensitive, mean-spirited--
Oh, drop it. This has nothing to do with Luke. This is about Rory.
This is not about Rory. This is about Luke. Don't you have an ounce of sensitivity in that thick head of yours or are you so mad at the entire world that you don't care who you hurt?
And I suppose we're still not talking about Rory?
Wow, second "Rory" in ten seconds. You sure have Rory on the brain. I wonder why that is.
You started this!
Is that why you came back here? Are you still hung up on her Jess ? Is that why you came back?
No.
Good. Because she is over you. She has moved on and she is very happy.
[to Gypsy] Please hurry up so I can get the hell out of here.
I second that.
Wow. I wonder where Demi and Ashton are sitting.
I think we're late.
We're not late.
Grandma said dinner starts at six.
Yeah, well that means seven.
In what universe?
They invite you at six knowing you won't be here until seven so dinner won't start until eight. Actually we're early. Oh, there they are. Hey. Hi Mom. Oh, that's a bad face.
Told you we were late.
What is Rory doing here?
Hi, Grandma.
You weren't supposed to bring Rory.
You're really helping the kid's self-esteem here, Mom.
You don't know one man that would be willing to spend the evening with you?
I thought you liked Rory.
We do like Rory but we're short of men.
Well so am I.
Honestly, Lorelai. It's not your looks that keep them away. Think about that.
Excuse me, should I stay, or--?
Of course you should stay. We can't do anything about that now. Come on, come on...
So on a wigged-out level of one to ten, Mom is at--
Frances Farmer?
Yeah.
Rory, what are you doing here?
Lorelai couldn't find a man.
You weren't specific, Mom. You didn't say, "Bring a man."
And if I had, you would have been able to find one? Rory, sit over there. Marjorie, Shawna, this is my daughter Lorelai and her daughter Rory. This is Marjorie and Shawna.
Hi.
Hello.
[Whispers to Emily] Who are Marjorie and Shawna?
[Whispers back] Richard and Jason's secretaries. Dull girls, like two rolling pins sitting across from you, but we were desperate.
Hello, Emily, Richard.
Ah, Jason.
You're late, Jason.
I know, I'm sorry but I got hung up talking to Feriman in the lobby.
Feriman is here?
Yes, and he's three drinks ahead of everybody else.
Oh, marvelous.
No, don't sit there!
Oh.
Sit next to Lorelai. Rory move over.
Why?
You two, pretend you're together.
What?
Emily, good idea.
Shawna, Marjorie, for God's sake, look like you belong here. [They helplessly try to smile and please her.] Oh yes, that's much better.
So who else is joining us?
No one. We brought one of Richard's coats to hang over the chair.
We're saying it's Marjorie's husband.
He's making the rounds and at about eight he'll get sick and have to leave.
Does everybody understand the story?
I think so. But then we'll have to hide his jacket. So I suggest I put it under my dress and pretend to be pregnant, then Jason can pretend to be the doctor, then Rory can dig a tunnel, and --
I might have known you'd turn this into something ridiculous, Lorelai.
Yeah, I wanna be the doctor.
Oh good Lord. And Jason, move closer to Lorelai. And for God's sake, you two, at least act like you like each other.
Hey, your mom said.
Hey, there you are.
Yes here I am, at my job. Will wonders never cease?
Major party happening outside.
So I hear.
You gotta see it.
Well, I'm sure you can see enough for the both of us.
Big fire, crazy punch, too. Seriously, man, come on out. You won't believe it.
No, T.J., actually, I will believe it, because, see, I live here, so I've seen this festival, oh let's say, about five thousand times.
Yes, I see your point. Okay, well, Liz and I are taking off right after the festivities, so maybe you can come out and say sayonara.
I'll come out as soon as I can.
Great. How long do you think?
How long I think what?
How long do you think you will be doing that?
I don't know.
Looks like you're almost done.
Well I'm not.
The stack is getting pretty small.
Look, I will be out soon, okay?
Okay. I am going to hold you to that.
I consider myself warned.

The importance cannot be overstated. Language is humanity's lifeline. That is why I thank each and every one of you for your loyal support of the Ephram Wordus Rare Manuscript Acquisition Foundation. Because without it, we would just be stuck rooting around Nag Hammadi.
Psst! I don't get it.
Me neither.
You go to Yale.
Well, I skipped Obscure Manuscript Humor 101.
[To Jason] Hey, why was that funny?
No -- no idea.
You were laughing.
Take a poll. No one in this room has any idea what this crazy old man is talking about.
What a bunch of poseurs.
...hundreds of literary artifacts which might otherwise have been lost.
How far do you think we can push this?
I'm not sure.
Dancing?
Possibly.
Stroll on the terrace?
Passable.
Making out in the coat-check room?
Oh, that's going to be tricky.
So, once again, I thank you and I hope you all have a lovely evening.
I'm going to go find Feriman.
I have to say hello to Babe Wellington.
Mom, how much longer do Jason and I have to pretend to be together?
Lorelai, don't do this to me. Until this evening is over, you are together and I don't want to discuss it again.
Fine.
[to Jason] I just secured us the coatroom.
Let's go.
I'm going to make out in the coatroom. Don't eat my chicken.
That's going on your tombstone.
Oh, hello. I didn't know you'd be here.
You look well.
Thank you. How is business?
Very good.
How's your golf game?
Well it certainly can't match yours but I'm catching up.
Well, when you're ready…
I'll give you a call.
Fine. Good to see you again.
Same to you.
Well, who was that?
My father.
Your father?
And you two have met before?
Yes, briefly. I believe there was an Aquaman party involved.
Oh, man. This business thing must have been really bad for you guys.
What do you mean?
I mean, that was so cold. You talked like you barely knew each other.
Oh, no, no, we've always been like that.
You're kidding.
No, actually, asking me about my golf game was actually a little too touchy-feely for me.
Wow, who would have thought I would ever put my mother next to someone and think, "warm?"
Jason, I just heard your father was here.
How could you possibly have found that out this quickly?
Well, news travels fast here. People talk. So, what did Floyd say?
Well--
Richard, Floyd was just here.
We know, Mom, we saw him.
He came by the table? What nerve.
How dare he talk to his son.
Be quiet, Lorelai.
If he's here he must have a motive.
That's right. He never cared about rare manuscripts before.
Hm. He must be trying to get information.
Richard, I don't think he had an agenda.
What was his body language like?
Well, he was breathing and standing. I think all signs point to alive.
What did he ask you about?
He asked me about my golf game.
Not the business?
No.
Oh, oh, oh. He's tricky.
He didn't ask about the business, Dad, okay?
I know he didn't ask about the business, Lorelai. That was deliberate.
So he wanted to know nothing on purpose? The fiend.
Please, stay out of it.
He is planning something. Jason, I think we should strategize.
Richard, I really don't think--
I have been doing this a lot longer than you have, my boy. If a man like Floyd Stiles comes over to you and does not ask about the business, you can be sure that something very big is coming.
Uh, I guess I have to go. If you'll excuse me, ladies.
Bye. Nobody was believing you two as a couple anyway.
[into walkie-talkie] This is Bird Dog One to Bird Dog Two. The southwest corner is secure.
I'm at the southwest corner, Kirk.
Then where the hell am I?
Well, look who finally came out of his cave.
Oh, Carrie. What a coincidence.
You remember Anna, Jill.
Hello, Anna. Hello, Jill.
We just came from the reunion so we're a little tipsy.
Ah, well, you know, drink water, and take some aspirin before you go to bed.
I told them that you're trying to pretend that you don't remember the night.
I don't remember the night.
I remember the night.
The whole reunion remembered the night
We all talked about it.
Terrific.
Everybody had a crush on Butch Danes in high school.
So serious, so intense.
So hot in those tiny little shorts.
Okay, I should go find Liz.
Oh, I'll help you find her.
Oh, no, I don't wanna break up the party.
Oh, well, there's always room for a foursome.
So twenty years later, none of you are married?
Oh, no, we're all married.
Oh, there's Liz.
They're not gonna run out of punch are they?
They never run out of punch.
Oh, okay, well, I should go.
Wait, we're all going to the Styx/REO Speedwagon/Journey concert next week. We have an extra ticket if you're interested.
Oh, wow. If it was just Styx and REO Speedwagon, I'd be there, but Journey freaks me out. Sorry. Enjoy the festival.
Oh, come on T.J.

Hey, I'm just telling it how it is. The last fair we went, the line was so long it blocked the fruit-ice stand. And traditionally the fruit-ice people are not the nicest people on the circuit but you block their stand and they really go crazy. They threw lemon rinds. But it didn't matter. Most people stayed and they bought plenty.
Well, people seem to like my stuff.
We're heading to Minnesota next month. Big fair there. And this time we're unveiling the booth.
The booth?
T.J. just built me the greatest booth. You should see it.

Well, you've gotta have a good booth. It's the first thing people see. Earrings are small. You don't know they're there until you're right up on them, but a booth and a nice sign? A person's standing at the jousting match, they turn around and,"Hey, look at that booth with the nice sign." They come over, take a look at Lizzie's stuff, and bam, they're hooked.
Well, Luke, nice of you to join us.
Oh hi, Luke, I didn't see you there.
Yeah, well, I heard you were leaving right after the festival, so--
I'm so glad that you came out.
See you later, Liz.
Can you believe this thing? It hasn't changed one bit since we were kids.
Yeah, same crazy gathering that Mom would take us to.
And then Dad after she died.
He hated it worse than we did. He only took us 'cause Mom liked it.
Of course, that Founder's Day punch…
Lethal.
The first time I ever threw up on booze it was Founder's Day punch.
That's a nice story.
Hey, listen, I'm sorry about Jess.
Boy, that statement could encompass a whole myriad of things.

I'm sorry I told you I wasn't in touch with him. It's just been the last six months he started calling and he asked me not to tell you, so I was trying to bond or something. I just mentioned the car to him. I didn't know he'd come back here and try to take it.
It's okay. It's his car and he should have it.
I'm just trying to make things better with us.
You should. It's fine.
I have a feeling about him. I think he's going to be okay. He's kinda like Dad, don't you think?
Oh, I don't know.
Oh, I do. I think he's like Dad. I want to thank you for everything that you did for him.
Well it never hurts to take a sh*t. At least you know you tried.
Sometimes things take a while before they sink in. It did with me. Sorry, I'm so boring tonight. I only had one cup of punch. Gary switched us over to club soda after that.
You're not boring. Who's Gary?
That's T.J.'s real name.
T.J.'s real name is Gary?
Yeah.
Gary?
Yeah.
How the heck did he get - Never mind. I heard him talking back there, Gary. It sounds like things are going pretty good.
They are. Really good.
Good, good.
Oh, hey, wait. I just made these last night. You can give them to your wife. Or Lorelai. Whoever...
Thanks.
Well, I'm going get my stuff together. We need to leave soon. Tell Gary I went back to your place.
I'll do that.
See you.
Gone for the rest of the night. We're stuck with the rolling pins. God! So boring!
I am starving.
What? The possibly beef and some sort of cream sauce did nothing to curb your appetite?
Do you want to start with burgers or do a cart-to-cart attack?
Well, there's two of us. I think we can accomplish both goals.
I'm going to get the burgers, you hit the carts.
I'll meet you by the bonfire.
Okay.
T.J.
Hi, you're here. Cool.
Yeah, so, Liz is back at my place getting your stuff, she just wanted me to tell you.
Okay. Thanks.

So look, I kind of heard you guys talking, and things seem to be going pretty good for Liz which is different, and a nice change, and I know that you guys are thinking about moving here, and I just wanted you to know, it's okay by me.
Okay. I didn't realize we needed your permission.

Oh, no. You don't. Maybe you misunderstood me here. I was just trying to say that I assumed because my sister has a history with guys, you know, that, you know, you were like the others. But, well, you seem like a pretty good guy.
Thanks. You're a dick.
So, I just heard the tail end of that conversation and I'm assuming you haven't changed your name to Richard?
Long, long story. I'll tell you later, but here's a teaser: the word Etch-A-Sketch comes up.
I'm hooked.
You're all dressed up.
Just for you.
You go somewhere?
Well, my parents had a charity event and they needed a chair filled and who fills a chair better than I?
No one comes to mind.
So, did Jess leave yet?
I stopped by Gypsy's earlier and she was just about done then, so probably.
No good-byes?
No. Liz has a feeling about him, though. She thinks he's gonna be fine.
He could be.
Yeah. Oh, hey, here.
Pretty.
Liz made them yesterday. She wanted you to have them.
Oh, great. Well, be sure to tell her thanks for me.
I will.
There.
Thank you for your business. Do not come again.
Not likely.
I get to leave first!
Rory, wait! Stop!
No, you don't get to walk away!
Hold on!
My town! I leave!
I just wanna--where are you going?
None of your business!
We look like idiots.
I don't care!
Stop running!
Stop following!
Oh, come on!
Go away, I'm leaving!
Rory, stop!
Why?
Because I wanna talk to you.
About what? What do you want to talk to me about?
When did you learn to run like that?

You know, I have actually thought about this moment. A lot. What would Jess say to me I ever saw him again? I mean, he just took off, no note, no call, nothing, how could he explain that? And then a year goes by. No word, nothing, so he couldn't possibly have a good excuse for that, right? I have imagined hundreds of different scenarios with a hundred different great last parting lines, and I have to tell you that I am actually very curious to see which way this is going to go.
Could we sit down?
No. You wanted to talk, so talk. What do you have to say to me?
I love you.
Oh, I love them. [petting the horses' noses]
Ooh, I love them, too. [also petting their noses]
With an unbridled passion. Good one, huh?
I love horse humor. [giggles]
These guys are the best I've got 'cause they're so sweet.
Hey, Michel, come on over. Meet our two new employees.
[standing far away] You know that I do not care for the animal kingdom.
Do you want me to hold them for you? 'Cause I've got a couple of others interested.
Oh, yes, definitely hold them. [dials number on cell phone]

Hi, Rory, it's me. How's school? You learning stuff? Listen, we have the horses, Desdemona and Cletus, and the first two rides have to be me and you. And hopefully, you're over the time that I took you for the pony ride, and the pony was old and just sort of stopped and laid down, and you sort of rolled off into the ditch. It's really not likely to happen again. I promise. So, call me, call me. [puts phone away as Tom walks by] Hey, Tom, how do you like our new horses?
Very fragrant. Follow me.
[to horse] He's very busy. Don't judge him too harshly.
Hey, guys, how's National Goof-off day going? That's what I thought. [Lorelai, Sookie and Michel join Tom] Now, we got downstairs hardware being delivered on Wednesday morning.
Yippee. [clapping hands with glee]
Yeah, it excites me too. So, I think it would be exciting to have one of you here to see that it's the right stuff. Otherwise, things would come to a crashing halt.
Oh boy, I got back to back meetings on Wednesday, and one of them is in Hartford. Sook?
I can be here. Oh no, I can't - Davey has a check up that morning.
Can you move it?
This doctor's really booked. But I can try.
That's okay. Michel?
I'm at the Tally Rand making the money that keeps me from having to stand at expressway off-ramps selling bags of cherries.
Okay. Oh well, I guess I can move some things around. I don't…
What is that?
That's your phone.
Who's phone? Our phone?
I installed it this morning. You wanted your phone up and running, right? To take reservations?
Oh, my God. [clapping hands]
Our first reservation.
Quick, quick, answer before they hang up.
Hello?
Dragonfly, Dragonfly.
Say Dragonfly Inn.

I mean, Dragonfly Iinn, hello. [pause] Why, yes! We are taking reservations. Our opening day is May 6th. [pause] May 8th and 9th, okay, great. Let me just check. Let me check. [pause] Okay. [She searches for a scrap of paper to write the information on. Unable to find anything else, she uses a gum wrapper.] You got it, and you're getting our best room. Let me just get your information here. Yes. Okay. And your number? Mm-hmm. 7873. Okay. Got your name. Got your number. Got you down for the 8th and 9th. Thank you, Mr. Turner. See you then. [hangs up] We're up and running.
We're up and running!
But you wrote it down on a gum wrapper.
So?
It's embarrassing. This is an historical document.
Who cares what she wrote it down on?
Big Red wrapper.
Juicyfruit would have been better?
Well, I'm going to go out and get a value pack for when things really start getting busy around here.

Mom, it's me, I left you a message at home, too. I love that you got horses. As far as that pony ride when I was a kid, you were forgetting one little tidbit there. That pony did not lie down.
